# Azure Mastery

> Azure Mastery is an iOS and iPadOS app for Microsoft certification exam preparation (Azure, AI, Data, Security, Power Platform, and GitHub). It uses on-device CoreML to predict your exam score (Exam IQ), build adaptive study plans, and track knowledge decay before exam day. 12,200+ practice questions cover 30 Microsoft certification exams. The app runs 100% offline with no tracking and no data collection.

Publisher: Moonbeam Alpha Ltd
Platform: iOS 18+, iPadOS 18+
Pricing: Free to download, with optional in-app purchases for full per-exam question banks. No subscription required for core study features.
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6760594569
Last updated: 2026-08-09

## Primary pages

- [Home — Azure Mastery](https://azuremastery.app/): Product overview, feature list, screenshots, and App Store link. Canonical entry point.
- [All exam pages](https://azuremastery.app/exams/): Hub listing every covered exam by family with links to each practice page.
- [About Azure Mastery](https://azuremastery.app/about/): Who publishes the app, what it does, and how it's built.
- [How we write and verify practice questions](https://azuremastery.app/how-we-write-questions/): How questions are written against Microsoft's published skills outlines, checked on every change, and watched weekly for drift.
- [How Exam IQ predicts your score](https://azuremastery.app/how-exam-iq-works/): How the on-device Exam IQ engine predicts a certification exam score from your practice record with an on-device CoreML model.
- [Retired Microsoft exams and what replaced them](https://azuremastery.app/exams/retired/): The five retired exams (AI-900, AI-102, DP-100, AZ-204, AZ-500), when each retired, and its current successor exam.
- [Support](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/support.html): User support, contact, and FAQ.
- [Privacy Policy](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/privacy.html): Data handling — none collected; everything runs on-device.
- [Terms of Use](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/terms.html): Standard EULA for in-app purchases.

## Per-exam landing pages

Every exam covered by the app has a dedicated landing page describing the exam, the in-app question count, the official Microsoft Learn skills outline, a suggested study plan, and cert-specific FAQs. Question counts are extracted directly from the app's bundled question banks. Each page ships a single `@graph` JSON-LD block linking 6 entities (WebPage, BreadcrumbList, EducationalOccupationalCredential, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, HowTo) for AI/AEO discoverability. The first 5 below are the most heavily-trafficked Azure exams and ship the deepest per-domain breakdowns.

### Azure infrastructure & solutions (5)

- [AZ-900 — Microsoft Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-900/): 364 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: cloud concepts (25–30%), Azure architecture and services (35–40%), Azure management and governance (30–35%). Skills outline updated 14 January 2026.

- [AZ-104 — Microsoft Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-104/): 481 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier sysadmin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five domains: identities and governance (20–25%), storage (15–20%), compute (20–25%), virtual networking (15–20%), monitoring (10–15%). Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-305 — Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-305/): 399 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier solution architect cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions plus case studies. Four design domains: identity/governance/monitoring (25–30%), data storage (20–25%), business continuity (15–20%), infrastructure (30–35%). Recommended Associate prerequisite: AZ-104. Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-204 — Developing Solutions for Microsoft Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-204/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. **⚠ Microsoft retired AZ-204 on 31 July 2026** — it can no longer be scheduled; the current AI cloud developer route is AI-200. Five developer domains: compute (25–30%), storage (15–20%), security (15–20%), monitor/troubleshoot/optimize (5–10%), connect/consume services (20–25%). Heavy on SDK code samples in C#/Python/JavaScript. Skills outline updated 14 January 2026.

- [AZ-400 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-400/): 467 in-app practice questions (largest single-cert bank). Expert-tier DevOps cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five DevOps domains: process/communications (10–15%), source control (10–15%), build/release pipelines (50–55%), security/compliance (10–15%), instrumentation (5–10%). Required Associate prerequisite: AZ-104 OR AZ-204. Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

- [AZ-500 — Microsoft Azure Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-500/): 346 in-app practice questions. **⚠ Microsoft retired AZ-500 on 31 August 2026** — it can no longer be scheduled; the successor is SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer). Associate-tier security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing identity and access (Entra, conditional access, PIM), securing networking (NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link, DDoS), securing compute/storage/databases, and managing security operations (Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Key Vault). Skills outline updated 22 January 2026.

- [AZ-700 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-700/): 569 in-app practice questions. Specialty-tier network engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing/implementing core networking (VNets, peering, hybrid), private access (Private Link, ExpressRoute, VPN), routing and load balancing (Application Gateway, Load Balancer, Front Door, Traffic Manager), and securing/monitoring networks. Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

### AI, Machine Learning & Copilot Agents (11)

- [AI-900 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-900/): 340 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-900 on 30 June 2026 and replaced it with AI-901; AI-900 can no longer be scheduled.

- [AI-901 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-901/): 572 in-app practice questions. Current replacement for retired AI-900; the Fundamentals credential does not expire and local exam pricing varies. 45-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Two assessed areas: identify AI concepts and responsibilities (40–45%); implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%). Requires foundational cloud/Azure knowledge and understanding Python examples. English exam updated 15 April 2026.

- [AI-102 — Designing and Implementing a Microsoft Azure AI Solution (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-102/): 334 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-102 on 30 June 2026; the current role-based Azure AI apps and agents route is AI-103.

- [AI-103 — Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-103/): 557 in-app practice questions for the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential. 100-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/manage an Azure AI solution (25–30%), generative and agentic solutions (30–35%), computer vision (10–15%), text analysis (10–15%), and information extraction (10–15%). Requires Python and Microsoft Foundry experience. Skills measured as of 16 April 2026.

- [AI-200 — Azure AI Cloud Developer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-200/): 220 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier AI cloud developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing cloud-native AI applications, embedding LLMs into Azure-hosted apps, integrating with Azure AI Search and storage, and operationalising AI workloads. Skills outline updated March 2026.

- [AI-300 — Microsoft Azure ML Operations Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-300/): 362 in-app practice questions (covers the ML Operations Engineer role). Associate-tier cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing the ML lifecycle on Azure ML — model training pipelines, registries, deployment to managed and Kubernetes endpoints, monitoring drift, and responsible-AI evaluation in production. Skills outline updated March 2026.

- [AI-500 — Microsoft Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-500/): 452 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier cert, launched in beta in 2026. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Four domains: architect multi-agent solutions (15–20%), develop multi-agent solutions in Azure (30–35%), evaluate, optimize, and monitor multi-agent solutions (20–25%), and secure, govern, and deploy multi-agent solutions (20–25%). Covers Microsoft Foundry, the Microsoft Agent Framework, orchestration patterns, A2A and MCP protocols, agent observability, and Microsoft Entra Agent ID.

- [AB-410 — Microsoft Intelligent Applications Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-410/): 424 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert with a 120-minute assessment for makers who build AI-powered business solutions in Microsoft Power Platform using Copilot, natural-language prompts, and low-code tools. Three domains: create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%), create intelligent applications (25–30%), and build business application logic and automation (40–45%). Microsoft's study guide was last updated 15 May 2026. Successor route for makers who previously targeted PL-200 — Microsoft replaced course PL-200T00 with AB-410T00.

- [AB-620 — Microsoft AI Agent Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-620/): 387 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert focused on designing and building integrated AI solutions in Copilot Studio. Three domains: plan/configure agent solutions (30–35%), integrate/extend agents (40–45%), and test/manage agents (20–25%). Official study guide updated 21 April 2026.

- [AB-650 — Microsoft AI Services Administrator Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-650/): 506 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier admin cert, launched in beta in 2026. 120-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: configure and manage Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (20–25%), govern and secure Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (40–45%), and manage and secure AI services in Microsoft 365 (35–40%). For Microsoft 365 administrators taking on Copilot, agent governance with Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Agent ID, and Microsoft Purview data security for AI.

- [AB-731 — Microsoft AI Transformation Leader](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-731/): 335 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier leadership cert (no-code), does not expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration (65-min seat), 30–40 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%), identify benefits/capabilities of Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%), identify an implementation and adoption strategy (20–25%). For business decision-makers, programme leads, and AI champions — not builders. Skills outline 2026.

- [AB-900 — Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-900/): 323 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 35–45 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify core features/objects of Microsoft 365 (30–35%), data protection and governance for M365 and Copilot (35–40%), basic admin tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%). For IT admins deploying and governing Copilot. Skills outline published May 2026.

- [AB-100 — Microsoft Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-100/): 443 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier architect cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates architecting multi-agent enterprise solutions with the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework, Microsoft Agent Framework, MCP extensibility, Computer Use, agent feed, and DSPM for AI. Skills outline published May 2026.

### Data (5)

- [DP-900 — Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-900/): 346 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates core data concepts (relational vs non-relational, OLTP vs OLAP), relational data on Azure (Azure SQL family), non-relational data on Azure (Cosmos DB, blob/file/table), and analytics workloads (Synapse, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI fundamentals). Skills outline updated 1 November 2024.

- [DP-100 — Designing and Implementing a Data Science Solution on Azure (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-100/): 350 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired DP-100 on 1 June 2026; it can no longer be scheduled.

- [DP-300 — Administering Microsoft Azure SQL Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-300/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier database administrator cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/implement data platform resources (15–20%), implement secure environment (20–25%), monitor/configure/optimize (20–25%), automation (15–20%), HA/DR (20–25%). Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

- [DP-700 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-700/): 336 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Microsoft Fabric data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains each weighted 30–35%: implement and manage an analytics solution (Fabric workspaces, Git and deployment pipelines, OneLake security, orchestration), ingest and transform data (full/incremental loads, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks, PySpark, T-SQL, KQL, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, Eventstream and Spark Structured Streaming), and monitor and optimize an analytics solution (alerts, error resolution, Lakehouse/Warehouse/Spark tuning). Requires SQL, PySpark, or KQL. Skills outline updated 21 July 2026.

- [DP-750 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Azure Databricks](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-750/): 442 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Azure Databricks data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Four domains: set up and configure an Azure Databricks environment (15–20%), secure and govern Unity Catalog objects (15–20%), prepare and process data (30–35%), deploy and maintain data pipelines and workloads (30–35%). Covers compute selection, Unity Catalog objects and governance (grants, row/column security, ABAC, lineage, Delta Sharing), Delta modelling and Lakeflow/Auto Loader ingestion, Spark optimisation (OPTIMIZE, VACUUM), and CI/CD with Databricks Asset Bundles. Requires SQL and Python. Skills outline updated 11 March 2026.

- [DP-800 — Microsoft Certified: SQL AI Developer Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-800/): 393 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SQL developer cert focused on AI-enabled SQL workloads (exam title: "Developing AI-Enabled Database Solutions"), renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration (120-min seat), 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: design and develop database solutions (35–40%) — advanced T-SQL, JSON, regex, fuzzy matching, graph queries, AI-assisted dev; secure/optimize/deploy (35–40%); implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%) — embeddings, vector indexes, RAG with `sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint`. Skills outline published 12 March 2026.

### Security, Compliance & Identity (5)

- [SC-900 — Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-900/): 397 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates security, compliance, and identity concepts; Microsoft Entra ID capabilities; Microsoft Defender XDR security solutions; and Microsoft Purview compliance solutions. Skills outline updated 7 November 2025.

- [SC-100 — Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-100/): 452 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier cybersecurity architect cert (single exam earns the credential, with prerequisite Associate cert). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 120-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing Zero Trust strategy and architecture, evaluating governance/risk/compliance technical strategies, designing security for infrastructure, and designing security for data and applications. Skills outline updated 27 April 2026.

- [SC-200 — Microsoft Security Operations Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-200/): 374 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SOC analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates mitigating threats with Microsoft Defender XDR (Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, Cloud Apps), mitigating threats with Microsoft Sentinel (KQL, analytics rules, watchlists, hunting), and managing security operations across the Microsoft security stack. Skills outline updated 16 April 2026.

- [SC-300 — Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-300/): 428 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier identity admin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates implementing identities in Microsoft Entra ID, implementing authentication and access management (conditional access, MFA, PIM, passwordless), implementing access management for apps, and planning/implementing identity governance. Skills outline updated 27 April 2026.
- [SC-500 — Microsoft Cloud and AI Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-500/): 432 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cloud and AI security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. The successor to AZ-500 (which Microsoft retired on 31 August 2026); beta from May 2026, exam expected July 2026. Validates managing identity, access, and governance (Entra ID, PIM, Key Vault, Azure Policy, RBAC); securing storage, databases, and networking (Defender for Storage, Azure SQL, NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link); securing compute and AI workloads (Defender for Servers/Containers, plus securing AI — Entra Agent ID, Defender for AI, AI Gateway for Foundry, Purview DSPM for Copilot); and managing and monitoring security posture (Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Security Copilot). Skills outline published May 2026.

### Power Platform (2)

- [PL-300 — Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-300/): 378 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier data analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates preparing data (Power Query M, data profiling), modelling data (star schemas, DAX measures, calculation groups, row-level security), visualising and analysing data (Power BI reports, dashboards, AI visuals), and deploying/maintaining assets (workspaces, deployment pipelines, refresh, sensitivity labels). Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.
- [PL-900 — Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-900/): 328 in-app practice questions. Fundamentals-tier low-code cert, never expires, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates the business value of Power Platform, managing the environment (Dataverse, security model, ALM pipelines), Power Apps (canvas, model-driven and code apps, plus AI-built apps), Power Automate (cloud and desktop flows), and building agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio (topics, knowledge sources, MCP tools, channels). Skills outline updated 24 July 2026.

### GitHub (2)
- [GH-300 — GitHub Copilot](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-300/): 356 in-app practice questions. Intermediate GitHub certification covering responsible AI use, Copilot features (IDE, Copilot CLI, Agent Mode, Edit Mode, MCP, Copilot Chat, code review, org-wide policies), Copilot data and architecture, prompt engineering and context crafting, developer productivity, and privacy, content exclusions, and safeguards.
- [GH-900 — GitHub Foundations](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-900/): 347 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier GitHub certification covering Git and GitHub basics, working with repositories, collaboration (issues, pull requests, discussions), modern development practices (GitHub Actions, Codespaces, Copilot), project management, privacy/security/administration, and the GitHub community.

## Guides

Free long-form study guides — exam-neutral advice grounded in the official Microsoft Learn skills outlines. Every guide article includes FAQ structured data, and the ten how-to guides also include study-plan structured data. Index: [Azure certification guides](https://azuremastery.app/guides/).

- [Which Microsoft certification should you get first?](https://azuremastery.app/guides/which-azure-certification-first/): Decision guide mapping roles (IT ops, security, data, AI, business) to the right entry certification and its associate-level follow-on.
- [How to pass AZ-900 Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-900/): Study plan, domain breakdown, hardest topics, and what to do after passing.
- [How to pass AZ-104 Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-104/): Six-week study plan, domain weights, hardest topics (networking, RBAC), and exam-day tactics.
- [How to pass SC-900 Security Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-sc-900/): Security, compliance, and identity fundamentals prep with next steps into SC-500/SC-200.
- [How to pass DP-900 Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-dp-900/): Core data concepts, relational vs non-relational, analytics, and the data career path.
- [How to pass AI-901 AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-901/): The AI-900 successor — AI workloads, generative AI, responsible AI, and the AI-103 path.
- [How to pass AI-103 Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-103/): All five skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the Foundry-based AI apps and agents exam.
- [How to pass AB-620 Copilot Studio AI Agent Builder](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ab-620/): All three skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the low-code Copilot Studio agent exam.
- [How to pass AB-100 Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ab-100/): All three skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the multi-agent architecture exam.
- [How to pass SC-500 Cloud and AI Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-sc-500/): All four skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for AZ-500's successor.
- [How to pass AI-200 Azure AI Cloud Developer](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-200/): All four skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the AI cloud back-end exam.
- [AZ-900 vs AZ-104](https://azuremastery.app/guides/az-900-vs-az-104/): Which Azure certification fits, whether you need both, and in what order.
- [SC-900 vs AZ-900](https://azuremastery.app/guides/sc-900-vs-az-900/): Security-first or cloud-first — how the two fundamentals exams differ and which to sit first.
- [AB-620 vs AB-410](https://azuremastery.app/guides/ab-620-vs-ab-410/): Copilot Studio agent builder or intelligent-app builder — credential, domains, exam format, and which to build first.
- [AI-103 vs AI-200](https://azuremastery.app/guides/ai-103-vs-ai-200/): AI apps and agents or AI cloud developer — credential, domains, exam format, and which layer to sit first.
- [SC-500 vs AZ-500](https://azuremastery.app/guides/sc-500-vs-az-500/): What changed when Microsoft retired AZ-500, how SC-500 compares, and what carries over if you already hold AZ-500.

## Core capabilities

- **Exam IQ**: On-device CoreML model that predicts your exam-day score with a confidence range from your practice record (accuracy by domain, coverage, mastery, consistency, recency).
- **Adaptive study plans**: The app picks your next session — weak-spot drills, knowledge-decay refreshes, mock exams — based on your current ability estimate per domain.
- **Aura first-week guidance**: Aura adapts the learner's next step throughout the first week and closes every study block with a concise, evidence-led recap.
- **Exam simulator**: Full-length, timed practice tests using blueprint-weighted question sets; Microsoft's live interface and exact item mix may differ.
- **Knowledge decay tracking**: Spaced-repetition signals flag topics where your retention has dropped before exam day, with targeted refresher sessions.
- **Question types**: Nine interactive formats for exam-style rehearsal, including multiple choice, multi-select, drag-and-drop ordering, hotspot, and case studies.
- **Answer Coach**: The explanation card shows the correct reasoning, option-by-option rationale where available, and the misconception, key distinction, and rule to remember. Learners can show explanations after each question or at the end of a practice test, then jump to missed answers with session notes kept ready. Authored guidance is always available; supported devices may optionally rewrite a note on-device only after grounding checks.
- **Offline-first**: Works fully without a network. No telemetry, no analytics on user behavior, no account required.
- **Apple ecosystem**: Native SwiftUI on iPhone and iPad; Live Activities for active study sessions; Apple Watch glance for streaks and XP.

## Differentiation

Azure Mastery is built for serious certification candidates who want to know *when they're ready* rather than just drilling questions. It is differentiated from generic flashcard apps by:

1. ML score prediction calibrated to Microsoft's pass thresholds, not a raw % correct.
2. Per-domain ability estimation — you see exactly which of an exam's domains is dragging your predicted score down.
3. Knowledge decay alerts so you don't lose old material while learning new domains.
4. Privacy-first computation — Exam IQ, Answer Coach, and study-plan generation run on-device; optional sync uses the learner's private iCloud account.

## /exams/ab-100/ — AB-100 Practice Questions — 443 Qs for AI Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Plan AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Design AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Deploy AI-powered business solutions (40–45%)
Q: How much does the AB-100 exam cost?
A: The AB-100 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; pricing varies by region). As an Expert-tier exam, AB-100 is rarely included in free-voucher promotions — if one appears around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, it's worth grabbing. Renewal itself stays free.
Q: Does the AB-100 certification expire?
A: Yes. Like Microsoft's other role-based certifications, AB-100 expires annually, with a free 25–30 question renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn available in the six-month window before expiry — scoped to whatever changed since you last certified (Foundry, Copilot Studio MCP features, Dynamics 365 orchestration, and similar). AB-900, the Fundamentals-tier exam, doesn't expire.
Q: What is the AB-100 retake policy if I fail?
A: 24 hours before your first retake, then 14 days for the second and third, capped at five attempts in any rolling 12 months with a fresh voucher each time. Given how broad AB-100's syllabus is, treat a fail as a signal to target the weakest domain specifically rather than rebooking immediately.
Q: What does the AB-100 exam format look like?
A: Like most Microsoft Certification exams, AB-100 has 40–60 questions in a mix of formats, with the exact timing confirmed at registration. It runs across a 100-minute session (120 minutes with seat time for admin), online or at a test centre, and scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. In Azure Mastery's AB-100 bank you'll practise a heavier share of multi-paragraph scenario questions than the associate-level agent exam banks, so you spend real time reading a business constraint before picking the architecture that fits it.
Q: How long should I study for AB-100?
A: Eight to twelve weeks if you already have hands-on time with at least one of Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, or Dynamics 365 Copilot. Give it three to four months if multi-agent orchestration is genuinely new — AB-100 expects you to design end-to-end solutions, not just describe the pieces.
Q: AB-100 vs AB-620 — which agent cert should I take?
A: Different altitudes. AB-620 certifies the maker who builds an agent in Copilot Studio. AB-100 certifies the architect who decides which platform an agent belongs on, how it's governed, and how the ALM and ROI case gets made across Copilot Studio, Foundry, and Dynamics 365 at once. Build the agent first; architect the estate second.
Q: AB-100 vs AI-103 vs AB-620 — how do the roles differ?
A: AI-103 is the code-first developer path (Python, Foundry). AB-620 is the Copilot Studio builder path (low-code agents). AB-100 sits above both as the architecture credential spanning every Microsoft AI surface. Get comfortable with an implementation credential before attempting the architecture-level exam.
Q: Do I need prerequisites before attempting AB-100?
A: Not formally, but AB-100 assumes it. Microsoft expects candidates to already hold AI-901-level knowledge, plus working experience with at least one of AI-102, AI-103, PL-200, PL-300, PL-400, PL-500, or AB-620. AB-100 tests architectural decisions across platforms you're assumed to already know individually — it isn't where most candidates start their Microsoft AI journey.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-100 prep?
A: The app is free to download with a free allowance of AB-100 questions. The full 443-question AB-100 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AB-100 practice work offline?
A: Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so a flight or offline commute won't interrupt your study streak. No account is required, and your data stays on-device unless you turn on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-410/ — AB-410 Practice Questions — 424 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Create intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Build business application logic and automation (40–45%)
Q: How much does the AB-410 exam cost?
A: Microsoft Associate exams typically cost USD $165, but pricing, currency, and taxes vary by country or region. Check the price shown when scheduling AB-410 through Microsoft Learn before purchasing. The certification must be renewed annually through Microsoft's free online renewal process.
Q: Does the AB-410 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AB-410 expire annually. Renewal is free through a short, unproctored online assessment on Microsoft Learn during the six-month eligibility window before expiration. Microsoft does not promise a fixed question count. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AB-410 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AB-410?
A: Allow four to eight weeks of focused study if you already build apps and flows in Microsoft Power Platform. Spend longer if Dataverse modelling, Power Fx, model-driven app design, or AI Builder prompts are new to you. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule the exam.
Q: AB-410 vs AB-620 — which builder cert?
A: Different surfaces. AB-410 is the Intelligent Applications Builder cert: you build Power Platform applications — Dataverse data models, model-driven and canvas apps, cloud flows — that consume agents, prompts, and AI models. AB-620 is the AI Agent Builder cert, focused on designing and extending the agents themselves in Microsoft Copilot Studio. AB-410 builds the application around the agent; AB-620 builds the agent. Many makers hold both.
Q: AB-410 vs PL-900 — which should I take first?
A: PL-900 first if Microsoft Power Platform is new to you. PL-900 is the Power Platform Fundamentals exam and stays conceptual — what Power Apps, Power Automate and Dataverse are for. AB-410 is the role-based exam where you configure the real artefacts: tables and relationships, forms and views, cloud flows, and AI Hub prompts. Makers new to the platform often use PL-900 as a foundation before AB-410.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-410 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-410 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 424 AB-410 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-410 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AB-410 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ab-620/ — AB-620 Practice Questions — 387 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Plan and configure agent solutions (30–35%)
  - Integrate and extend agents in Copilot Studio (40–45%)
  - Test and manage agents (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AB-620 exam cost?
A: The AB-620 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; pricing varies by region). Watch for occasional free-voucher promotions around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite — Microsoft doesn't run them year-round. Renewal itself is free.
Q: Does the AB-620 certification expire?
A: Yes — AB-620 expires annually like every Microsoft Associate certification. Renewal is a free, 25–30 question assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six-month window before expiry and scoped to whatever changed in the outline since you last certified. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AB-620 retake policy if I fail?
A: 24 hours before your first retake, then a 14-day wait for the second and third. Microsoft caps you at five attempts in any rolling 12 months, and each attempt needs its own voucher.
Q: What does the AB-620 exam format look like?
A: Like most Microsoft Certification exams, AB-620 has 40–60 questions in a mix of formats, with the exact timing confirmed at registration. It runs as a 100-minute session (120 minutes with seat time for admin), taken online with a proctor or at a test centre, and scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. In Azure Mastery's AB-620 bank you'll practise single-answer and multi-select multiple choice plus a noticeable share of yes/no and matching items, so you're not just drilling straight recall.
Q: How long should I study for AB-620?
A: Four to eight weeks if you already build with Copilot Studio or the wider Power Platform; longer if Power Fx, Dataverse, MCP, or agent lifecycle management are unfamiliar. The exam leans heavily on the Integrate and extend domain (40–45%), so prioritise hands-on time there.
Q: AB-620 vs AI-103 — different agent roles?
A: Different platforms for different builders. AB-620 is Microsoft Copilot Studio — a low-code environment for building agents with topics, generative answers, and Power Platform integrations. AI-103 is Microsoft Foundry — a code-first platform for Python-based agents, tool calling, and multi-agent orchestration. AB-620 is for Copilot Studio builders; AI-103 is for app developers. Many enterprises use people certified in both.
Q: AB-620 vs AI-901 — which should I take first?
A: Take AI-901 first if AI concepts are genuinely new to you — it's the Fundamentals exam and assumes no build experience. AB-620 is role-based and assumes you can already navigate Copilot Studio, Dataverse, and Power Platform environments.
Q: Do I need a Copilot Studio licence to prepare for AB-620?
A: Not to use Azure Mastery, but hands-on practice matters more for AB-620 than for most exams. Microsoft offers trial access to Copilot Studio — check the current terms on Microsoft Learn — and building topics, agent flows, and knowledge-source connections there pairs well with Azure Mastery's scenario questions, rather than relying on question practice alone.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-620 prep?
A: The app is free to download with a free allowance of AB-620 questions. The full 387-question AB-620 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AB-620 practice work offline?
A: Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so a flight or offline commute won't interrupt your study streak. No account is required, and your data stays on-device unless you turn on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-650/ — AB-650 Practice Questions — 506 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-23
Exam domains:
  - Configure and manage Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (20–25%)
  - Govern and secure Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (40–45%)
  - Manage and secure AI services in Microsoft 365 (35–40%)
Q: How much does the AB-650 exam cost?
A: Microsoft prices AB-650 by the country or region where the exam is proctored and has not published a single flat fee for the beta — check the official exam page for your local price when you register. During a beta, Microsoft sometimes opens a short discounted-registration window (announced on the Microsoft Learn blog) with a discount code for a limited number of seats. The certification renews annually with a free online assessment once you're certified, so there is no recurring fee.
Q: Does the AB-650 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AB-650 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills-outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AB-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AB-650 retake policy if I fail?
A: AB-650's beta status changes this for now. If you don't pass a beta exam, Microsoft has you wait until the exam goes live before you can retake it — the usual 24-hour and 14-day retake windows don't apply during the beta window. Once AB-650 is fully live, Microsoft's standard retake policy takes over: a 24-hour wait before your first retake, 14-day waits before the second and third, and a cap of five attempts per rolling 12 months. Each attempt requires a new voucher.
Q: How long should I study for AB-650?
A: Allow four to eight weeks of focused study if you already administer Microsoft 365 tenants and Microsoft Entra ID day to day. Spend longer if Microsoft Purview data protection, Conditional Access, Agent 365, or Microsoft Entra Agent ID are new to you. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule the exam.
Q: AB-650 vs AB-620 — administer or build?
A: Different roles over the same agent estate. AB-620 is the AI Agent Builder Associate credential — the maker-role exam for designing, integrating, and testing agents inside Microsoft Copilot Studio. AB-650 is the administrator-role exam: it's about governing whatever agents your organisation ends up with, wherever they were built, across the wider Microsoft 365 tenant — licensing, identity, Defender and Purview protection, the agent registry, and Agent 365 monitoring. A Copilot Studio maker and a Microsoft 365 administrator often sit on the same team; AB-620 and AB-650 map to those two different jobs.
Q: AB-650 vs AB-900 — do I need the fundamentals exam first?
A: AB-900 (Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals) is the conceptual on-ramp — it stays at the "what is it and why does it matter" level across core Microsoft 365 objects, data protection concepts, and basic Copilot and agent administration. AB-650 is the associate-level exam built on top of that: it expects you to actually configure the tenant settings, identity policies, and agent governance controls, and to defend the trade-offs between similar-looking options. AB-900 isn't a formal prerequisite for AB-650, but it's a solid foundation if Microsoft 365 administration is new to you.
Q: AB-650 vs SC-300 — how much identity overlap is there?
A: Some overlap, different depth. SC-300 (Identity and Access Administrator) goes far deeper into Microsoft Entra identity architecture — hybrid identity, external identities, application integration, and identity governance at a specialist level. AB-650 covers the identity surface a Microsoft 365 administrator actually touches day to day — users, groups, administrative units, Conditional Access, and Privileged Identity Management — plus the newer agent identity model built on Microsoft Entra Agent ID, which SC-300 does not cover. Candidates who own both Microsoft 365 and deep identity architecture often hold both certifications.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-650 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-650 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 506 AB-650 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-650 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AB-650 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ab-731/ — AB-731 Practice Questions — 335 Qs for AI Leadership (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%)
  - Identify benefits, capabilities, and opportunities for Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%)
  - Identify an implementation and adoption strategy for Microsoft's AI apps and services (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AB-731 exam cost?
A: AB-731 is a Beginner-tier credential. The voucher is USD $99 in the United States; in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft regularly offers free vouchers via Microsoft Build, Microsoft Ignite, and free virtual training events, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers before booking. Pricing is subject to change and varies by country/region — see the AB-731 certification page for current local pricing.
Q: Does the AB-731 certification expire?
A: No. AB-731 is a Beginner-tier credential and, like other Beginner-tier Microsoft credentials (AI-901, AB-900, SC-900), it does not expire. Once earned, the credential is yours permanently. This is in contrast to Associate, Expert, and Specialty certifications, which require annual renewal on Microsoft Learn.
Q: What is the AB-731 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AB-731 retake failures usually come from underestimating the strategy and governance domain — most candidates over-study Copilot product features and under-study ROI framing, licensing models, and adoption frameworks.
Q: How long should I study for AB-731?
A: Most business decision-makers pass AB-731 after three to five weeks of focused study, assuming working familiarity with Microsoft 365 and basic generative-AI concepts. AB-731 is a no-code leadership exam — you do not need to build agents — but you do need to articulate ROI, licensing models, responsible-AI principles, and adoption frameworks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready; don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-620 — which is right for me?
A: Different jobs entirely. AB-731 is the leadership credential — for business decision-makers driving AI transformation across teams: framing ROI, choosing between build/buy/extend, championing responsible AI, and running adoption programmes. AB-620 (AI Agent Builder Associate) is the maker credential — for low-code builders shipping agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio with topics, generative answers, knowledge sources, and channel deployments. Pick AB-731 if your job is to lead change; pick AB-620 if your job is to build. Many programme leads take both.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-900 — what's the difference?
A: Different audiences. AB-900 (Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals) is the IT admin's Fundamentals exam — admin centres, Purview governance, licensing, agent approval flows. AB-731 (AI Transformation Leader) is the business leader's exam — ROI, adoption strategy, responsible AI, build/buy/extend decisions, AI council governance. AB-900 administers Copilot; AB-731 leads the AI transformation. Programme leads sometimes take both for full coverage of admin governance and business strategy.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-731 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-731 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 335 AB-731 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-731 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AB-731 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ab-900/ — AB-900 Practice Questions — 323 Qs for Copilot Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-05
Exam domains:
  - Identify the core features and objects of Microsoft 365 services (30–35%)
  - Understand data protection and governance tasks for Microsoft 365 and Copilot (35–40%)
  - Perform basic administrative tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%)
Q: How much does the AB-900 exam cost?
A: AB-900 is a Fundamentals-tier exam. The voucher is USD $99 in the United States; in the UK it's typically around £75. Microsoft regularly offers free vouchers via Microsoft Build, Microsoft Ignite, and free virtual training events for Fundamentals certifications, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers before booking. Fundamentals certifications do not expire, so there is no annual renewal cost.
Q: Does the AB-900 certification expire?
A: No. AB-900, like other Microsoft Fundamentals certifications (AZ-900, AI-901, SC-900, DP-900), does not expire. Once earned, the credential is yours permanently. This is in contrast to Associate and Specialty certifications which require annual renewal on Microsoft Learn.
Q: What is the AB-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AB-900's Fundamentals tier means questions are broader than they are deep, so most retake failures come from skipped Purview / Defender XDR content rather than M365 admin centre topics.
Q: How long should I study for AB-900?
A: Most candidates pass AB-900 after two to four weeks of focused study, assuming basic Microsoft 365 admin familiarity. If Microsoft 365 admin centres and Microsoft Entra are new to you, plan for six weeks — the exam expects you to recognise admin-centre objects (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, M365), Purview surfaces (Information Protection, DLP, Insider Risk, DSPM for AI), and Defender XDR features. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready; don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher.
Q: AB-900 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: Different scopes. SC-900 (Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals) is the broad Microsoft security overview — Entra, Defender, Purview, compliance, identity. AB-900 is narrower and more practical: it focuses on Microsoft 365 Copilot administration, with security and Purview coverage scoped to the Copilot / agent threat surface (DSPM for AI, sensitivity-label flow into Copilot grounding, oversharing in SharePoint). If you already passed SC-900, AB-900 will feel like an extension. If you're starting fresh and your role is M365-Copilot-focused, take AB-900 directly first.
Q: AB-900 vs AB-731 — what's the difference?
A: Different altitudes. AB-900 is the hands-on-governance Fundamentals cert: it expects you to identify Microsoft 365 admin-centre objects, Purview governance surfaces, and day-to-day Copilot administration controls (licensing, usage analytics, agent approval flow). AB-731 (AI Transformation Leader) is an Associate-tier strategy cert — it expects you to reason about organisation-wide AI adoption, Microsoft Foundry, and responsible AI at a leadership level, not configure individual admin centres. AB-900 administers what's already rolled out; AB-731 plans the rollout and the governance strategy behind it. IT admins usually want AB-900 first; those setting AI strategy across a team or organisation are better served starting with AB-731.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 323 AB-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AB-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ai-102/ — AI-102 Retired Exam & AI-103 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Plan and manage an Azure AI solution (20–25%)
  - Implement generative AI solutions (15–20%)
  - Implement an agentic solution (5–10%)
  - Implement computer vision solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement natural language processing solutions (15–20%)
  - Implement knowledge mining and information extraction solutions (15–20%)
Q: Can I still take the AI-102 exam?
A: No. Microsoft retired AI-102 and the Azure AI Engineer Associate certification on 30 June 2026. The exam can no longer be scheduled.
Q: What replaced AI-102?
A: AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. It leads to the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential and assesses Python, Microsoft Foundry, generative and agentic solutions, vision, text analysis, and information extraction.
Q: What happens if I already earned Azure AI Engineer Associate?
A: A certification earned before retirement remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-102 and its renewal assessment are retired, so the exam cannot be retaken or newly earned.
Q: Are AI-102 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for Azure AI services, generative AI, vision, language, search, and document intelligence. New candidates should study the current AI-103 outline and use its exam-specific bank.
Q: What is the current path after AI-102 retirement?
A: AI-901 is the current Azure AI Fundamentals exam, and AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. AI-102 content remains useful as historical reference, but new candidates should use the AI-901 and AI-103 outlines rather than planning an AI-102 certification path.
Q: What replaced the retired AI-102 and DP-100 routes?
A: Microsoft replaced the retired AI-102 route with AI-103 for Azure AI apps and agents, and identifies AI-300 as the replacement for the retired DP-100 data-science route. AI-103 focuses on application and agent development; AI-300 focuses on operationalizing machine learning and generative AI systems.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-102 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-102 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 334 AI-102 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AI-102 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-102 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ai-103/ — AI-103 Practice Questions — 557 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Plan and manage an Azure AI solution (25–30%)
  - Implement generative AI and agentic solutions (30–35%)
  - Implement computer vision solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement text analysis solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement information extraction solutions (10–15%)
Q: How much does the AI-103 exam cost?
A: The AI-103 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; regional pricing varies). Because AI-103 is a role-based Associate exam rather than a Fundamentals-tier one, Microsoft rarely bundles it into free promotional vouchers — watch for occasional offers around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite instead. Renewal itself is free.
Q: Does the AI-103 certification expire?
A: Yes — like every Microsoft Associate certification, AI-103 expires annually. Renewal is a free, 25–30 question assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six-month window before expiry, and it's scoped to whatever changed in the outline since you last certified. AI-901, the Fundamentals-tier exam, doesn't expire — only role-based certifications like AI-103 do.
Q: What is the AI-103 retake policy if I fail?
A: You can retake AI-103 24 hours after a failed first attempt; the second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft allows a maximum of five attempts in any rolling 12 months, and every attempt needs its own voucher.
Q: What does the AI-103 exam format look like?
A: Like most Microsoft Certification exams, AI-103 has 40–60 questions in a mix of formats, with the exact timing confirmed at registration. It runs as a 100-minute session (120 minutes with the seat time Microsoft allows for exam admin), taken online with a proctor or at a test centre, and scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. In Azure Mastery's AI-103 bank you'll practise several of those formats yourself — single-answer and multi-select multiple choice, ordering and matching items, and a small number of linked case studies.
Q: How long should I study for AI-103?
A: Plan for several weeks of focused study if you already write Python and have touched Azure AI services before; extend that if Microsoft Foundry, agents, or multimodal AI are new territory. The exam expects working familiarity across five distinct domains, so breadth of practice matters as much as depth in any one area. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you judge when you've closed that gap.
Q: AI-103 vs AI-102 — different roles?
A: AI-102 retired on 30 June 2026. AI-103 replaced it as the current Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate exam, and it reflects how far the underlying platform has shifted toward Microsoft Foundry, agentic patterns, and multimodal content — not just a renamed version of the old outline.
Q: AI-103 vs AI-901 — which should I take first?
A: Take AI-901 first if generative AI and Microsoft Foundry are unfamiliar concepts — it's the Fundamentals exam and assumes no coding. AI-103 assumes you can already write Python and expects hands-on familiarity with Foundry projects, agent tools, retrieval, and evaluation. Candidates with existing development experience sometimes skip AI-901 and go straight to AI-103.
Q: Do I need real Foundry or Python experience before I start?
A: Not to begin studying, but AI-103 is written for candidates who already develop with Python and have touched Azure services — it isn't an intro-to-AI exam. If you're newer to development, working through Microsoft Foundry's own quickstarts alongside Azure Mastery's practice questions will close that gap faster than question practice alone.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-103 prep?
A: The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AI-103 questions to try Answer Coach, the readiness gauge, and the adaptive plan before you commit. The full 557-question AI-103 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AI-103 practice work offline?
A: All of it — question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction run on-device, so a flight or an offline commute doesn't interrupt your study streak. No account is required, and your data stays on your device unless you turn on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ai-200/ — AI-200 Practice Questions — 220 Qs for AI Developer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Develop containerized solutions on Azure (20–25%)
  - Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services (25–30%)
  - Connect to and consume Azure services (20–25%)
  - Secure, monitor, and troubleshoot Azure solutions (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AI-200 exam cost?
A: The AI-200 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. AI-200 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AI-200 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AI-200 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AI-200 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AI-200?
A: Allow four to eight weeks of focused study if you already develop on Azure. Spend longer if Python, Azure SDKs, containerized applications, Cosmos DB or PostgreSQL vector search, messaging, or KQL-based troubleshooting are new to you. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule the exam.
Q: What prior experience does AI-200 assume?
A: AI-200 assumes you already work across the full AI-solution lifecycle on Azure — implementation, deployment, security, monitoring, and troubleshooting — with practical comfort in Azure and third-party SDKs, containerized applications, and Python. It expects you to already know your way around Azure data management services and messaging, not to learn them from the study guide alone. If containers or vector-capable databases are genuinely new to you, budget extra time beyond the usual four-to-eight-week window.
Q: AI-200 vs AI-103 — different roles?
A: Different emphases. AI-200 validates back-end Azure development for AI solutions, including containers, data services, messaging, security, monitoring, and troubleshooting. AI-103 focuses on developing AI apps and agents with Python and Microsoft Foundry. AI-200 is cloud-platform and service integration; AI-103 is model, agent, retrieval, and AI-application implementation.
Q: AI-200 vs AI-300 — which next?
A: AI-200 first. AI-200 is the AI Cloud Developer Associate cert — building the platform that AI workloads run on. AI-300 is the ML Operations Engineer Associate cert — running and operating ML and generative-AI systems in production (MLOps and GenAIOps). AI-200 is upstream of AI-300 in most roles. Take AI-200 to build the platform, AI-300 to operate models and pipelines on top of it.

## /exams/ai-500/ — AI-500 Practice Questions — 452 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-23
Exam domains:
  - Architect Multi-Agent Solutions (15–20%)
  - Develop Multi-Agent Solutions in Azure (30–35%)
  - Evaluate, Optimize, and Monitor Multi-Agent Solutions (20–25%)
  - Secure, Govern, and Deploy Multi-Agent Solutions (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AI-500 exam cost?
A: Microsoft prices AI-500 by the country or region where the exam is proctored and has not published a single flat fee for the beta — check the official exam page for your local price when you register. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. The certification renews annually with a free online assessment, so there is no recurring fee.
Q: Does the AI-500 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Expert certifications including AI-500 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AI-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AI-500?
A: Allow six to ten weeks of focused study if you already build agentic solutions on Microsoft Foundry with Python. Spend longer if orchestration frameworks, Model Context Protocol, agent identity and RBAC, or evaluation and observability tooling are new to you. This is an expert-level exam that expects hands-on production experience, not just familiarity — Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule it.
Q: AI-500 vs AI-103 — which do I need?
A: Different tiers and different scope. AI-103 (Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate) validates building AI apps and single agents on Microsoft Foundry with Python — models, retrieval, vision, speech, and one agent talking to its own tools. AI-500 (Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert) is the expert tier above it: architecting, orchestrating, evaluating, and securing systems where multiple agents coordinate in production, including Microsoft Agent Framework orchestration patterns, Agent2Agent and MCP integration, and per-agent identity and guardrails. The dependency is also formal: Microsoft lists the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate certification (earned via AI-103) as a required prerequisite, so you receive the Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert credential only once you hold it and pass AI-500.
Q: AI-500 vs AB-100 — architect or engineer?
A: Different roles at a similar level. AB-100 (Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect) is the business-architecture view of agentic AI — ROI analysis, build-vs-buy across Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, and Power Platform, governance, and ALM, aimed at architects who plan agentic solutions across an enterprise. AI-500 is the hands-on engineering expert exam — designing, coding, evaluating, and securing the multi-agent systems themselves, with Microsoft Agent Framework, MCP servers, orchestration patterns, and agent identity. Pick AB-100 if you're deciding which agentic patterns a business should adopt; pick AI-500 if you're the one building and running them.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-500 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 452 AI-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-500 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ai-900/ — AI-900 Retired Exam & AI-901 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Describe Artificial Intelligence workloads and considerations (15–20%)
  - Describe fundamental principles of machine learning on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of computer vision workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of Natural Language Processing (NLP) workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of generative AI workloads on Azure (20–25%)
Q: Can I still take the AI-900 exam?
A: No. Microsoft retired AI-900 on 30 June 2026, so it can no longer be scheduled. AI-901 is now the exam route to the Azure AI Fundamentals credential.
Q: What replaced AI-900?
A: AI-901 replaced AI-900 on 1 July 2026. It remains the route to Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals and adds a more implementation-oriented focus on Microsoft Foundry and Python examples.
Q: What happens if I already passed AI-900?
A: An Azure AI Fundamentals credential earned through AI-900 remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-900 itself is retired and cannot be retaken.
Q: Are AI-900 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for core AI, machine-learning, vision, language, and responsible-AI concepts. New candidates should study the current AI-901 outline and use the AI-901 bank for exam readiness.
Q: AI-900 vs AI-102 — which should I take first?
A: AI-900 first, unless you already build AI applications professionally. AI-900 is the conceptual map: it teaches you the vocabulary (image classification vs object detection, key phrase extraction vs entity recognition, regression vs classification, the Foundry model catalog) without expecting you to write code. AI-102 is the role-based Associate exam — it expects hands-on Python, REST API calls against Azure AI services, and prompt-engineering against Azure OpenAI. Most candidates pass AI-900 in a few weeks, then spend two to three months on AI-102.
Q: Is AI-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — that's a large part of the audience. Microsoft positions AI-900 for both technical and non-technical candidates: solution consultants, sales engineers, technical PMs, business stakeholders evaluating Azure AI procurement, and anyone wanting a credible answer to "which Azure AI service should we use for this?" The exam doesn't ask you to write Python. It asks you to recognise scenarios — "which Azure AI service is best suited for redacting PII from a document?" or "which guiding principle of responsible AI applies here?" — and pick the correct option.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 340 AI-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AI-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

  - Manage Azure identities and governance (20–25%)
  - Implement and manage storage (15–20%)
  - Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20–25%)
  - Implement and manage virtual networking (15–20%)
  - Monitor and maintain Azure resources (10–15%)
Q: How much does the AZ-104 exam cost?
A: The AZ-104 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. AZ-104 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AZ-104 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AZ-104 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AZ-104 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-104?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with prior Azure experience, or longer if they are new to administration. Practise identity and governance, storage, compute, virtual networking, and monitoring in the portal and with Azure CLI, PowerShell, and Bicep so you can choose and apply the right administration method. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready.
Q: What prior experience does AZ-104 assume?
A: AZ-104 assumes familiarity with operating systems, networking, servers, and virtualisation, plus hands-on experience with PowerShell, Azure CLI, the Azure portal, and ARM templates or Bicep files. It isn't written for someone with zero IT background — Microsoft expects a working administrator, not a beginner learning what a virtual machine is. If those fundamentals are genuinely new, AZ-900 first (or general IT experience) will make AZ-104 far more approachable.
Q: AZ-104 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: If you have less than six months of hands-on Azure experience, take AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) first — it builds the conceptual map AZ-104 assumes you already have. If you have a year or more of practical Azure work, you can skip AZ-900 and go straight to AZ-104. Most hiring managers care about AZ-104 specifically; AZ-900 is often dropped from CVs once AZ-104 is on it.
Q: AZ-104 vs AZ-305 — which next?
A: Pass AZ-104 first. AZ-104 is the Associate-level operational cert; AZ-305 is the Expert-level architectural cert. AZ-305 assumes you already understand Azure operations (the AZ-104 material) and adds requirements gathering, capacity planning, governance design, and choosing between competing service options. Most architects hold both — AZ-104 to prove they've done the work, AZ-305 to prove they can design it.

## /exams/az-305/ — AZ-305 Practice Questions — 399 Qs for Azure Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions (25–30%)
  - Design data storage solutions (20–25%)
  - Design business continuity solutions (15–20%)
  - Design infrastructure solutions (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-305 exam cost?
A: The AZ-305 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. AZ-305 is the single exam required for the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert certification — the predecessor pair AZ-303 and AZ-304 were retired in March 2022. The Expert-tier certification also requires annual renewal (free, online via Microsoft Learn).
Q: Does the AZ-305 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Expert certifications — including Azure Solutions Architect Expert (which AZ-305 unlocks) — expire annually. Renewal is free: a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain active in solution-architect work.
Q: What is the AZ-305 retake policy if I fail?

Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AZ-305 has a higher fail rate than AZ-104 because it tests design judgement (which service for which requirement) over recall — many candidates need a second attempt.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-305?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks of focused study, even if you have already passed AZ-104. AZ-305 tests judgement more than recall — you're given a scenario and asked which combination of Azure services satisfies it. That style takes longer to internalise than the AZ-104 "how do I configure X" style. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 730 or higher with reasonable confidence; AZ-305 is unforgiving of borderline scores.
Q: AZ-305 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AZ-104 first. Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) is the operational certification required alongside AZ-305 to earn Azure Solutions Architect Expert. AZ-305 is the expert-level design exam and assumes you already understand Azure operations.
Q: Do I need other exams alongside AZ-305?
A: AZ-305 is the expert-level exam for Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert. You must also hold Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, earned through AZ-104. Passing AZ-305 alone does not award the expert credential.

Q: How much does the AZ-400 exam cost?
A: The AZ-400 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite — worth checking your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers. The DevOps Engineer Expert tier also requires annual renewal (free, online via Microsoft Learn) once earned.
Q: Does the AZ-400 certification expire?

Q: What is the AZ-400 retake policy if I fail?
