Q: How long should I study for AZ-400?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks for AZ-400, even if you already hold AZ-104 or AZ-204. AZ-400 covers an enormous service surface — Azure Pipelines AND GitHub Actions, both Azure DevOps AND GitHub repositories, Bicep AND ARM templates, Azure Key Vault AND GitHub Secrets, plus security scanning, monitoring, branching strategies, and progressive deployment patterns. The build/release pipelines domain alone is 50–55% of the exam. Don't book until Azure Mastery's readiness gauge shows roughly 730 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: AZ-400 vs AZ-305 — which Expert cert should I take?
A: Pick the one that matches your role. AZ-400 is for SREs, platform engineers, and developers who own CI/CD; AZ-305 is for architects designing the systems those pipelines deploy. They are complementary and both can use Azure Administrator Associate as a prerequisite. AZ-305 does not accept Azure Developer Associate as an alternative.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AZ-400 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-400 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 467 AZ-400 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AZ-400 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AZ-400 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/az-500/ — AZ-500 Retired Exam & SC-500 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Secure identity and access (15–20%)
  - Secure networking (20–25%)
  - Secure compute, storage, and databases (20–25%)
  - Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-500 exam cost?
A: The AZ-500 voucher was USD $165 in the United States, with regional pricing. AZ-500 was retired by Microsoft on 31 August 2026 and can no longer be booked; candidates should sit SC-500, the current Cloud and AI Security Engineer exam, instead.
Q: Does the AZ-500 certification expire?
A: AZ-500 and the Azure Security Engineer Associate certification retired on 31 August 2026. Microsoft states that renewal assessments are no longer available after a certification retires; already-earned Azure Security Engineer Associate credentials remain valid on your transcript. If you are starting now, prepare for SC-500 instead.
Q: What is the AZ-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-500?
A: AZ-500 was retired by Microsoft on 31 August 2026 and can no longer be booked, so study SC-500, its current successor, instead. SC-500 keeps the identity and access, platform protection, and security operations core while adding cloud and AI workload security — build hands-on familiarity with Entra, Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Key Vault, Azure networking, and workload protection either way.
Q: AZ-500 vs AZ-104 — should I do AZ-104 first?
A: Microsoft strongly recommends AZ-104 first, and it shows. AZ-500 assumes you already know how Azure compute, networking, and storage work day-to-day — it's the security overlay on top of that knowledge. If you've never deployed a VM or configured a VNet outside of fundamentals, take AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) first; you'll save weeks on AZ-500 prep. If you have a year or more of hands-on Azure ops, you can skip AZ-104 and go straight in. Some employers want both anyway.
Q: AZ-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. AZ-500 is the Azure Security Engineer cert — it's about hardening Azure resources end-to-end. SC-200 is the Security Operations Analyst cert — it's about running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, with much heavier focus on M365 and incident triage workflows. If your day job is securing Azure workloads, AZ-500. If it's running detection-and-response across the Microsoft estate, SC-200. Many Cybersecurity Architect Expert candidates hold both, with SC-900 as the connective fundamentals.

A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 346 AZ-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

## /exams/az-700/ — AZ-700 Practice Questions — 569 Qs for Network Engineer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Design and implement core networking infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design, implement, and manage connectivity services (20–25%)
  - Design and implement application delivery services (15–20%)
  - Design and implement private access to Azure services (10–15%)
  - Design and implement Azure network security services (15–20%)
Q: How much does the AZ-700 exam cost?
A: The AZ-700 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. AZ-700 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AZ-700 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AZ-700 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AZ-700 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-700?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with prior Azure networking experience. Build and troubleshoot virtual networks, hybrid connectivity, routing, private access, application delivery, and network security in a lab; know when to choose services such as Virtual WAN, ExpressRoute, Application Gateway, Front Door, Azure Firewall, and Private Link. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready.
Q: AZ-700 vs AZ-104 — should I do AZ-104 first?
A: Microsoft strongly recommends AZ-104 first, and it shows. AZ-700 assumes you already know how Azure compute, storage, and the basic VNet model work day-to-day — it's the deep-network specialism on top of that knowledge. If you've never deployed a VM with a public IP or set up a basic NSG outside of fundamentals, take AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) first; you'll save weeks on AZ-700 prep. If you're already a working network engineer crossing into Azure, you can skip AZ-104 and go straight in.
Q: AZ-700 vs SC-500 — which is the right network/security pairing?
A: They overlap around cloud-network protection, but the roles differ. AZ-700 expects you to design and operate connectivity, including hybrid networks, routing, private access, and application delivery. SC-500 applies security controls across cloud and AI workloads, including identity, posture, threat protection, and workload security. Take AZ-700 for network engineering depth; add SC-500 when your remit includes end-to-end cloud security.

## /exams/az-900/ — AZ-900 Practice Questions — 364 Qs for Fundamentals (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Describe cloud concepts (25–30%)
  - Describe Azure architecture and services (35–40%)
  - Describe Azure management and governance (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-900 exam cost?
A: The AZ-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the AZ-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as AZ-104 or AZ-305, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: What is the AZ-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If cloud computing is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: AZ-900 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AZ-900 first, almost always. AZ-900 is designed as the on-ramp to AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator). It takes a few weeks to prepare for and doesn't expire; AZ-104 takes two to three months and requires hands-on PowerShell and CLI knowledge. Most people pass AZ-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.
Q: Is AZ-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — that's exactly who AZ-900 is designed for. Account managers, project managers, sales engineers, and finance partners all sit AZ-900 to qualify for Microsoft Partner Network roles. The exam doesn't expect you to write a PowerShell script. It expects you to explain concepts such as region pairs, the shared responsibility model, and when a hybrid cloud is appropriate.
Q: What prerequisites does AZ-900 assume?
A: AZ-900 has no formal prerequisites — Microsoft designed it as the common entry point into the Azure ecosystem. That said, some background in an area of IT (infrastructure, databases, or software development) makes the material easier to absorb quickly, since you'll already have working knowledge of an environment to map Azure's concepts onto. If you're coming from a completely non-technical background, expect the low end of the one-to-two-week study estimate to stretch out.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AZ-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 364 AZ-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.

Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the DP-700 certification expire?
A: Yes. DP-700 earns the Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate, expert, and specialty certifications it must be renewed every year. Renewal is free — you pass a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before your certification expires. (This is different from Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900, which never expire.)

Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: DP-700 vs DP-750 — different data engineering roles?

DP-700 is for engineering analytics solutions end to end in Microsoft Fabric — Lakehouse, Warehouse, Eventhouse, pipelines, and Dataflows Gen2, transforming with SQL, PySpark, and KQL. DP-750 is for building production data-engineering solutions on Azure Databricks — Unity Catalog, Auto Loader, Lakeflow, and Delta Lake. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on which platform your organisation runs.
Q: Is DP-700 a technical, hands-on exam?
A: Yes. DP-700 expects you to reason about real data-engineering work in Microsoft Fabric — writing and debugging T-SQL, PySpark, and KQL; designing full and incremental load patterns; working with Delta tables, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, and pipelines; and optimising Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Spark performance. It's a working data engineer's exam, not a conceptual overview. If you want a non-technical, vocabulary-level data certification first, look at DP-900 (Azure Data Fundamentals) as an on-ramp.

Q: Does the DP-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as DP-300 or AZ-104, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: What is the DP-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for DP-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If cloud computing is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: What prior experience does DP-900 assume?
A: Very little. Microsoft doesn't expect database-administration experience or hands-on SQL — just basic familiarity with what a spreadsheet or database is, and a general sense of what "cloud" means. If you can describe why a company might store data in more than one place, you have enough of a starting point; the exam teaches the Azure-specific vocabulary as you study.
Q: DP-900 vs PL-900 — which should I take first?
A: They test different things and neither is a prerequisite for the other, so pick based on your role. DP-900 covers data concepts and Azure's data services — relational vs non-relational, analytics workloads, Power BI as a visualisation layer. PL-900 covers the low-code Power Platform itself — Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse, and Copilot Studio agents. A data analyst or engineer heading toward DP-300 or AI-300 should start with DP-900; a business user or maker heading toward PL-300 should start with PL-900. Many candidates who work across both simply sit them in either order.
Q: Is DP-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — Microsoft positions DP-900 for both technical and non-technical candidates. Data analysts about to step into Power BI work, software engineers crossing into a data role, and product managers responsible for analytics architecture all sit DP-900. The exam doesn't ask you to write SQL queries. It asks you to recognise scenarios — "which Azure SQL service for this workload?" or "which storage tier for this access pattern?" — and pick the correct option.

A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 346 DP-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/gh-300/ — GH-300 Practice Questions — 356 Qs for GitHub Copilot (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Use GitHub Copilot Responsibly (15–20%)
  - Use GitHub Copilot Features (25–30%)
  - Understand GitHub Copilot Data and Architecture (10–15%)
  - Apply Prompt Engineering and Context Crafting (10–15%)
  - Improve Developer Productivity with GitHub Copilot (10–15%)
  - Configure Privacy, Content Exclusions, and Safeguards (10–15%)
Q: How much does the GH-300 exam cost, and how long is it?
A: The GitHub Copilot exam is roughly USD $99, though the exact price varies by region. GH-300 runs about 90 minutes and you need 700 out of 1000 to pass. It's delivered through Microsoft's exam platform, but the certification itself is owned and maintained by GitHub. Check the official GitHub Copilot page for current pricing and any active promotions before you book.
Q: Does the GH-300 GitHub Copilot certification expire?
A: GitHub credentials are valid for two years and are renewed by re-examination — so once you pass GH-300 you stay certified for two years, then re-take the exam to keep the credential current. The certification is delivered by Microsoft but owned and maintained by GitHub, which sets this two-year validity.
Q: Who is the GH-300 GitHub Copilot exam for?
A: GH-300 is an intermediate-level certification for developers and technical team members who already use GitHub Copilot day to day and want to prove real, applied expertise. It assumes GitHub fundamentals and experience in at least one programming language. This is not a beginner exam — it validates working knowledge of Copilot's features, data flows, prompt engineering, and responsible-use practices.
Q: Does GH-300 cover using GitHub Copilot responsibly?
A: Yes. "Use GitHub Copilot Responsibly" is the first domain, weighted 15–20%. It tests the risks and limitations of generative AI, ethical and responsible AI use, how to identify potential harms and their mitigations, and — critically — why you must validate Copilot's output before trusting it. Expect scenario questions about biased or insecure suggestions and how a professional handles them.
Q: How much of GH-300 is prompt engineering?
A: Prompt engineering and context crafting is its own domain, weighted 10–15%. GH-300 tests how you structure a prompt, how Copilot determines context, the difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting, and the core principles of writing prompts that produce useful, relevant suggestions. It pairs closely with the data-and-architecture domain, which explains how your prompt is processed and turned into a suggestion.
Q: How many GH-300 practice questions does Azure Mastery include?
A: Azure Mastery ships with 356 GH-300 practice questions, each mapped to one of the six official GitHub Copilot domains — from responsible AI and Copilot features to data and architecture, prompt engineering, developer productivity, and privacy with content exclusions. Core study runs on-device and works offline; optional sync uses your private iCloud account.

  - Understand Privacy, Security, and Administration (10–15%)

Q: How much does the GH-900 exam cost?
A: The GitHub Foundations exam is USD $99, a price set by GitHub rather than Microsoft's standard certification pricing. GH-900 is delivered through Microsoft's exam platform, but the certification itself is owned and maintained by GitHub. Check the official GitHub Foundations page for current pricing and any active promotions before you book.
Q: Does the GH-900 GitHub Foundations certification expire?
A: Yes. Unlike Microsoft's own Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 or AI-901, which never expire, GitHub Foundations is valid for two years from the date you pass. To stay certified after that, you re-take the GH-900 exam. This two-year validity is set by GitHub, which owns and maintains the certification.
Q: What is the GH-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: GH-900 follows the standard Microsoft exam-delivery retake policy. The first retake is allowed after a 24-hour wait. Second, third, fourth, and fifth retakes each require a 14-day wait, with a cap of five attempts in any 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new exam booking.
Q: How long should I study for GH-900?
A: If you already use GitHub day to day — opening pull requests, reviewing branches, working with issues — one to two weeks of focused revision is usually enough. If GitHub is new to you, plan for three to four weeks so the seven domains, from Git basics to GitHub Actions and security, have time to stick. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: GH-900 vs AZ-900 — what's the difference?
A: GH-900 (GitHub Foundations) validates collaboration on GitHub: Git, repositories, pull requests, branches, GitHub Actions, Issues and Projects, security features, and the open-source community. AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) validates cloud concepts and core Azure services. They're independent credentials in different product families — GH-900 is owned by GitHub and is valid for two years, while AZ-900 is owned by Microsoft and never expires. Many DevOps-minded candidates earn both.
Q: Is GH-900 worth taking if I'm not a developer?
A: Yes — GH-900 is explicitly designed for non-developers as well as developers. Project managers, technical writers, product owners, and team leads all sit GH-900 to prove they can collaborate effectively on GitHub. The exam doesn't ask you to write code. It expects you to explain concepts such as the GitHub Flow, how pull requests link to issues, what branch protection rules do, and when to use a fork versus a template.

Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Prepare the data (25–30%)
  - Model the data (25–30%)
  - Visualize and analyze the data (25–30%)
  - Manage and secure Power BI (15–20%)
Q: How much does the PL-300 exam cost?
A: The PL-300 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. PL-300 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the PL-300 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including PL-300 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the PL-300 retake policy if I fail?

Q: How long should I study for PL-300?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with regular Power BI practice. Spend hands-on time in Power Query, semantic modelling, DAX, report design, analysis, sharing, and workspace security; the exam rewards choosing the right modelling and visualisation approach for a scenario. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready.
Q: PL-300 vs DP-900 — which should I take first?
A: DP-900 first if you don't have a working understanding of relational vs non-relational data, transactional vs analytical workloads, or the SQL family on Azure. DP-900 (Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals) builds that grounding. PL-300 assumes you already know the difference when it asks scenario questions about DirectLake vs DirectQuery vs Import, or about Microsoft Fabric semantic models. If you already do data-analyst work day-to-day, you can skip DP-900 and go straight to PL-300.
Q: PL-300 vs DP-300 — different roles?
A: Different angles on the data stack. PL-300 is the analyst-side cert — it focuses on building Power BI reports from data: Power Query M, DAX, visualisations, governance and sharing. DP-300 is the operational DBA cert — it focuses on running Azure SQL workloads: HA/DR, performance tuning, security, automation. The two complement each other in larger BI teams; small teams often have one person doing both.

## /exams/retired/ — Retired Microsoft Exams & Successors | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Q: Can I still book a retired exam?
A: No — once Microsoft retires an exam, Pearson VUE stops scheduling new sittings for it. All five exams on this page, including AZ-500 (retired 31 August 2026), are now closed to new bookings.
Q: Does my credential expire when the exam retires?
A: No. A credential you earned by passing a Microsoft exam stays valid and stays on your Microsoft Learn transcript after the exam itself retires — retirement stops new bookings, it doesn't undo a credential you've already earned.
Q: Can I renew a credential from a retired exam?
A: No. When Microsoft retires an exam, its renewal assessment retires with it, so the credential cannot be renewed after the retirement date. It stays on your transcript as earned. To hold a current credential in that area, sit the successor exam listed above.
Q: Do retired questions still count in the app?
A: Azure Mastery keeps each retired exam's question bank in the app as reference material for anyone who bought it, or passed the exam before it retired. It isn't counted in the app's advertised exam or question totals.
Q: Which retired exam maps to which successor?
A: AI-900 to AI-901, AI-102 to AI-103, DP-100 to AI-300, AZ-204 to AI-200, and AZ-500 to SC-500. The table above lists each one with its retirement date.

## /exams/sc-100/ — SC-100 Practice Questions — 452 Qs for Cyber Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-05
Exam domains:
  - Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities (20–25%)
  - Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for applications and data (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-100 exam cost?
A: The SC-100 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-100 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-100 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-100 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the SC-100 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-100?
A: Most candidates pass SC-100 after six to ten weeks of focused study, assuming an Associate-level prerequisite is already passed. SC-100 is design-oriented, so much of the prep is reading and pattern recognition rather than command memorisation — practice scenario reasoning until you can articulate why each distractor is wrong. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready; don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: What's the SC-100 prerequisite?
A: You can register for and sit SC-100 with no prior certification. What Microsoft withholds is the Cybersecurity Architect Expert credential itself: to earn it, you must also hold — or pass within a year of SC-100 — at least one of three Associate-level certifications: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500), Security Operations Analyst Associate (SC-200), or Identity and Access Administrator Associate (SC-300). Once you have both, both certifications appear on your Microsoft Learn profile.
Q: SC-100 vs AZ-305 — which next for an architect?
A: Different architectural lenses. SC-100 is the security architect cert — design Zero Trust, ransomware resilience, SecOps strategy, identity governance. AZ-305 is the solutions architect cert — design data, infrastructure, business continuity, and identity/governance/monitoring. The two overlap on identity and governance design, but SC-100 goes much deeper on security and AZ-305 covers a broader Azure surface. Many senior architects hold both.
Q: How is SC-100 different from an Associate-level security exam?
A: Associate exams such as SC-200 and SC-300 test whether you can configure and operate a named product correctly. SC-100 tests whether you can design the strategy those products serve — picking between Microsoft Sentinel automation vs Defender XDR-native response, or the enterprise access model vs legacy AD tiering, for a stated set of business constraints. Multiple options in an SC-100 scenario can be technically valid; the exam is scored on choosing the one that best satisfies the constraints given.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-100 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-100 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 452 SC-100 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-100 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

  - Perform threat hunting (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-200 exam cost?
A: The SC-200 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-200 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-200 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-200 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)

Q: How long should I study for SC-200?

Q: SC-200 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?

SC-200 is the role-based Associate exam: it expects you to investigate incidents in Defender XDR and write KQL hunting queries. Most candidates pass SC-900 in a few weeks then spend two to three months on SC-200.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-500 — different security roles?
A: Different angles on Microsoft security. SC-500 implements security controls across cloud and AI workloads; SC-200 runs detection, investigation, hunting, and incident response in Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. Choose SC-500 for cloud security engineering and SC-200 for security operations.
Q: Do I need to know KQL before starting SC-200?
A: Not on day one, but plan to learn it early — threat hunting is 20–25% of the exam and Kusto Query Language shows up across the other two domains too, in custom detection rules and advanced-hunting queries. Start with reading and modifying existing KQL (joins, parse operators, time windows) before writing queries from scratch; the exam tests whether you can pick the right table and interpret a result more than raw syntax recall.

## /exams/sc-500/ — SC-500 Practice Questions — 432 Qs for Cloud Security (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Exam domains:
  - Manage identity, access, and governance (20–25%)
  - Secure storage, databases, and networking (25–30%)
  - Secure compute (20–25%)
  - Manage and monitor security posture (20–25%)
Q: Is SC-500 replacing AZ-500?
A: Yes. SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer) is the direct successor to AZ-500 (Azure Security Engineer), which was retired by Microsoft on 31 August 2026. The SC-500 beta opened in May 2026, with full training and exam available from July 2026. SC-500 keeps the core Azure security-engineering content of AZ-500 and expands the role to cover securing cloud and AI workloads — including Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Foundry, and Defender for AI. Candidates should now prepare for SC-500 instead of AZ-500.
Q: How much does the SC-500 exam cost?
A: The SC-500 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-500 is an Associate certification and requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-500 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-500 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. (Fundamentals certifications such as SC-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the SC-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-500?
A: Most candidates pass SC-500 after four to eight weeks of focused study, assuming some prior Azure and Microsoft Entra experience. If cloud security is genuinely new to you, plan for two to three months — the exam expects hands-on knowledge of Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Entra ID, and Key Vault, not just concepts. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready; don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: What prior experience does SC-500 assume?
A: SC-500 assumes hands-on experience administering Azure and hybrid environments — compute, network, and storage — plus strong familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID and some exposure to Microsoft 365 administration. It isn't a from-scratch security course: Microsoft expects you to already operate the infrastructure you're being asked to secure. If you're new to Azure administration, working through AZ-104 material first (or the free AZ-900 fundamentals) will close that gap faster than jumping straight into security-specific practice.
Q: SC-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. SC-500 is the Cloud and AI Security Engineer cert — it's about implementing security controls across identity, storage, networking, compute, and AI workloads. SC-200 is the Security Operations Analyst cert — it's about running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, with heavier focus on detection, investigation, and incident response across the Microsoft 365 estate. If your day job is securing cloud and AI workloads, SC-500. If it's running detection-and-response, SC-200. Many Cybersecurity Architect (SC-100) candidates hold both, with SC-900 as the connective fundamentals.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-500 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 432 SC-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-500 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-500 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/sc-900/ — SC-900 Practice Questions — 397 Qs for Security Basics (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-05
Exam domains:
  - Describe the concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra (25–30%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (35–40%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-900 exam cost?
A: The SC-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it's typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the SC-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, SC-900, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as SC-200 or SC-300, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: What is the SC-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If security and compliance concepts are genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: SC-900 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: Neither depends on the other, so pick based on which vocabulary you need first. SC-900 teaches Microsoft's security, compliance, and identity stack — Zero Trust, Microsoft Entra, the Defender product family, Sentinel, Purview compliance. AZ-900 teaches general Azure fundamentals — regions and availability zones, core compute and networking services, pricing, and governance tools like Azure Policy. If your role is security-adjacent, start with SC-900; if you're new to Azure generally, start with AZ-900. Many candidates who work across both sit both, in either order, since they don't overlap much.
Q: Is SC-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — Microsoft positions SC-900 for both technical and non-technical candidates. Business stakeholders evaluating Microsoft security procurement, IT generalists adjacent to security, and students entering the field all sit SC-900. The exam doesn't ask you to configure Conditional Access or write KQL. It asks you to recognise scenarios — "which Microsoft Defender product covers this surface?" or "which Purview tool addresses this compliance requirement?" — and pick the correct option.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 397 SC-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.
